symmetricContinuousZeroSet.conclusion: Cauchy-Schwarz equality implies D(u)=d(u)*e for a constant unit vector e on each cell. Continuity and d>0 propagate the same e across a connected active curve. Constant d therefore makes paired curves translations with matching parameter tangents.
formalCellArgument: A nonnegative continuous integrand with zero integral vanishes everywhere on a positively weighted cell.
With D(u)=a+u*b and d(u)=d0+u*delta_d, squared-norm equality gives the three coefficient identities.
Thus b=(delta_d/d0)*a and e=a/d0 is unit. At every shared endpoint D=d*e with d>0, so adjacent e are identical.

effects: Admits contracted chords and provides no compression push.
Positive d makes r=0 an interior point of a constant-zero slack region; energy, gradient and Hessian there are zero if the implementation branches before radial normalization.
The r=d transition is generally C1 but not C2; active/slack Hessian selection at equality requires an explicit policy.
For affine D and d>0, tension/slack intervals are determined by the quadratic |D|²-d²; endpoint-only classification is insufficient.
Active-set crossing fractions can be irrational. A rational-only implementation must enclose and bound unresolved crossing slivers, rather than silently round roots and omit their contribution.
Within a strictly taut interval r>d, derivatives match the tensile part of the symmetric radial spring. Moving active-set boundaries carry zero energy and first-gradient boundary terms.
